newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via four-day systems.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via four-day systems.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to temporarily add reserves to the banking system on Friday via over-the-weekend system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
Due to the Labor Day holiday on Monday when all U.S. markets will be closed, the over-the-weekend operation will cover four days.
The Fed is facing a huge daily add need estimated at between $6.5 billion and $8 billion around Labor Day.
The Fed already injected reserves on Thursday with six-day fixed system RPs.

"The Fed is likely to add reserves via over-the-weekend systems, with a small possibility of five-day systems to match (the duration of) Thursday's operation," said senior economist Astrid Adolfson at MCM MoneyWatch.
Ahead of the 1130 EDT/1530 GMT usual intervention time, federal funds changed hands at 5-1/4 percent, on target.
